name: Joinery & Fit-Out (Doors, Windows, Wardrobes, Kitchens, Architectural Metal)

activities: door/window sub-frames and bucks built into blockwork/partitions
fixing grounds for skirting and panelling
sequence.note: Structural fixing points for heavy joinery are set at first fix inside the wall build-up, not retrofitted.

sequence.stage: S2 - Wait for wet trades & finishes
activities: hold delivery/install of finished joinery until plaster, screed, tiling and first-coat paint are complete and dry
sequence.note: Timber and finished cabinetry are moisture-sensitive; installing before wet works dry causes warping, staining and delamination.
Door undercuts and thresholds are set to the FINISHED floor level, so flooring datum must be known/laid.

activities: template and fit worktops after carcasses set
sequence.note: Kitchen/vanity carcasses must be set before plumbing and electrical second-fix so services terminate into them.

activities: fixing to structure/finished floor with sealed penetrations
sequence.note: Balustrade fixings into waterproofed or finished substrates use approved sealed details.
Ironmongery and fine adjustment are second-fix; door closers/access-control coordinate with MEP/security.

typical_relationships.before: wet trades (plaster, screed, tiling, first-coat paint) dry
typical_relationships.reason: moisture warps and stains timber and board joinery; installing into a wet room guarantees replacement
door undercut, threshold and skirting height reference the finished floor; guessing the datum causes binding doors or gaps
wardrobes, storage walls and worktops need concealed structural fixing set during wall build
taps, wastes, sockets and appliances terminate into the cabinetry; services before carcasses land in the wrong place
units mount onto finished walls; fixing first blocks the tile/paint plane and traps the finish behind furniture
handles, closers and hardware fit after decoration so paint does not foul moving parts

interfaces.requirement: wet works complete and dried; finished floor datum established before doors, skirting and cabinetry
kitchen and vanity carcasses set and services coordinated so sockets, taps, wastes and appliance connections terminate into the joinery; sequence carcass -> MEP termination -> worktop/appliance
joinery/balustrade fixings into wet-area or tanked substrates use approved sealed penetration details, not open drilling
finished floor laid or level agreed so thresholds, undercuts and skirting land correctly
door hardware (closers, mag-locks, access control, door position switches) coordinated with fire and security second fix and commissioning

commissioning_dependencies: fire/smoke door sets certified and door hardware commissioned with fire alarm interface
testing_requirements: operational check of doors, drawers, hinges under load
moisture content of timber at install
typical_exceptions: off-site prefabricated pods/rooms deliver joinery pre-installed, compressing on-site sequence
glazed partitions/screens are a specialist package overlapping facade
fire-rated and acoustic door sets carry certification hold-points beyond standard doors
loose/FF&E furniture is a separate post-handover package, not fixed joinery
evidence: Joinery is a moisture-gated second-fix trade whose defining interfaces are finished-floor datum, concealed first-fix blocking, and the carcass-before-MEP-termination handshake for kitchens/vanities. Fire-door certification and hardware-to-security coordination are universal. Generalized across sectors; no project-specific content.
